Phase 0 — Planning · nothing here is funded yet

An open door

An open door — and behind it, seven questions that open more. Tell us what you are looking for, and we will show you the paths that exist today and the ones we are building together.

This is not paperwork and there is nothing to prove here. It is a door, and you can walk through it at your own pace, skip any part of it, or leave it and come back on a better day. Some doors are open today; others are being built.

What is honest about where we are

  • Phase 0: 0 people housed, no funds raised, no housing available today — and no waitlist position to gain or lose.
  • The entity that will hold this work is not formed yet. Fiscal sponsorship → independent 501(c)(3), pending owner confirmation and legal counsel validation.
  • Nothing on this page is a promise. The listings below are real and open today; everything about our own program is a framework, not a commitment.
  • No one is enrolled by a web page. Answers here decide nothing about you, and a free help program never turns anyone away for answering honestly.
Open the seven doorsFind free help right now

One thing belongs at the top, before any question: if someone is hurting you, this page can wait. These doors are open right now, whether or not you walk any of ours.

If someone is hurting you, you never have to explain anything here.

You can leave this page at any time, answer nothing, and come back later, or never. These doors are open right now, whether or not you continue. They are free and confidential.

  • Center for Community Solutions — 24/7 Crisis Hotline (San Diego)

    Call 1-888-385-4657

    A confidential 24/7 crisis hotline in San Diego. Someone answers, day or night.

    Source: https://ccssd.org/ · Checked 2026-10-08

  • National Domestic Violence Hotline

    Call 1-800-799-7233, or text START to 88788

    Free, confidential, 24/7, in many languages. thehotline.org has a quick-exit button and ways to keep your visit private.

    Source: https://www.thehotline.org/ · Checked 2026-10-08

  • San Diego Humane Society — Safety Net Foster Program

    Call 619-299-7012

    Temporary care for your animals if you are leaving a domestic violence situation, so you never have to choose between your safety and your animal. Reunification is the goal.

    Source: https://sdhumane.org/services/temporary-pet-care/ · Checked 2026-09-05

Open today — these exist right now

Real San Diego programs, free to use, with the day we last checked each one. A badge tells the truth: open, closed, or worth a call before you travel.

  • 2-1-1 San Diego

    Open

    Always open; not a waitlist

    A free 24-hour phone and online service that connects you to housing, food, health, and other help.

    How to reach it: Dial 2-1-1 or search the database at 211sandiego.org

    Call 2-1-1Visit 2-1-1 San Diego

    Source: https://211sandiego.org/ · Checked 2026-09-04

  • HUD - Assistance Animal Rights under the Fair Housing Act

    Right in effect - federal enforcement narrowed May 2026

    Honesty flag: HUD's FHEO enforcement guidance (May 22, 2026) pursues animal-accommodation complaints only for animals individually trained to perform disability-related tasks - untrained ESAs are no longer prioritized by HUD enforcement, though Fair Housing Act / Section 504 obligations and private legal action still exist

    Under the Fair Housing Act, a housing provider must let you keep an assistance animal - a trained service animal or an emotional support animal - as a reasonable accommodation, even in no-pets housing, with no pet deposits or breed/size limits, with only narrow legal exceptions.

    How to reach it: Ask your housing provider in writing for a reasonable accommodation; if denied, file a complaint with HUD's Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity office at (800) 669-9777

    Call (800) 669-9777Visit HUD

    Source: https://www.hud.gov/helping-americans/assistance-animals · Checked 2026-09-05

  • San Diego Housing Commission - Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers

    Waitlist closed

    Closed Feb 1, 2026; watch portal for reopening

    A federal rent voucher that helps low-income households pay rent in private apartments.

    How to reach it: Check the SDHC waitlist portal at waitlist.sdhc.org for reopening announcements

    Call (619) 578-7777Visit San Diego Housing Commission

    Source: https://waitlist.sdhc.org/ · Checked 2026-09-04

  • Housing Authority of the County of San Diego (HACSD) - Rental Assistance

    Waitlist closed

    County-run rent help, including Section 8 vouchers, for areas outside the cities of San Diego and Chula Vista.

    How to reach it: Call HACSD rental assistance or check sandiegocounty.gov rental assistance page before applying

    Call (858) 694-4801Visit Housing Authority of the County of San Diego (HACSD)

    Source: https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/hcd/rental_assistance.html · Checked 2026-09-04

  • Project-Based Voucher Buildings (County / SDHC)

    Waitlist closed

    Availability varies per building; confirm individually

    Rent help tied to specific apartment buildings so tenants pay less rent each month.

    How to reach it: Call 2-1-1 or the housing authority to ask about any open building waitlists

    Visit Project-Based Voucher Buildings (County / SDHC)

    Source: https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/hcd/rental_assistance.html · Checked 2026-09-04

  • SDHC Moving Home Rapid Re-Housing (Housing First San Diego)

    Confirm current status

    Referral-based via Coordinated Entry, not open application

    Short-term rent help plus case management to move people off the street into housing fast.

    How to reach it: Call 2-1-1 to get connected to Coordinated Entry and ask about rapid re-housing

    Call (619) 578-7777Visit SDHC Moving Home Rapid Re-Housing (Housing First San Diego)

    Source: https://www.sdhc.org/homelessness-solutions/ · Checked 2026-09-04

  • San Diego Humane Society - Safety Net Foster Program

    Open

    Limited capacity, case-by-case; $30 microchip/license fees at reclaim; no visits during foster; extensions past 30 days not guaranteed

    Free temporary foster homes for your pet while you deal with housing insecurity, domestic violence, or a hospital stay, so you can keep your pet instead of giving it up; SDHS provides all care supplies and aims to reunite you within 90 days.

    How to reach it: Call 619-299-7012 to request the program application; staff follow up within about 72 hours

    Call 619-299-7012Visit San Diego Humane Society

    Source: https://sdhumane.org/services/temporary-pet-care/ · Checked 2026-09-05

  • 2-1-1 San Diego - Pet-Friendly Shelter and Housing Line

    Open

    City of San Diego confirms its contracted shelters and JFS Safe Parking allow domestic pets

    A free 24-hour phone line and online database that helps you find pet-friendly shelters, safe parking lots, and other housing help across San Diego County, so your pet can come with you.

    How to reach it: Dial 211 (or visit 211sandiego.org) and ask for pet-friendly shelters, safe parking, and pet-inclusive housing options

    Call 211Visit 2-1-1 San Diego

    Source: https://sdhumane.org/resources/pet-inclusive-housing-support/ · Checked 2026-09-05

  • MTS Reduced Fares - Seniors and Riders with Disabilities

    Open

    Cheaper bus and trolley fares for seniors, Medicare riders, and riders with disabilities.

    How to reach it: Fill out the MTS reduced-fare short or long form and visit the Transit Store

    Call 619-595-5636Visit MTS Reduced Fares

    Source: https://www.sdmts.com/fares · Checked 2026-09-04

Not sure where to start? Dial 2-1-1 — free, 24 hours a day. Every listing above is also on the free help finder, verified but not guaranteed.

Opening soon — we are building these with you

Nothing below is funded or running yet. It is written down honestly so you can see what is coming, and so your answers can shape what gets built first.

  • Phase 0 — not yet funded; framework, not a promise

    The Seed Program cohort path

    Twelve small starter cohorts of 5–25 people, each receiving the whole six-pillar system at once — housing, health, food, hygiene, regenerative income, and travel. Nothing is launched and no one is housed yet.

    Read the Seed Program

  • Phase 0 — not yet funded; framework, not a promise

    Animal-friendly homes

    Wellness animals are requirements in this program, not extras: pet-friendly housing is a program rule, pet setup and monthly pet care are budgeted lines, and settling-in padding covers people and animals.

    See the build spec

  • Phase 0 — not yet funded; framework, not a promise

    The Regenerative Commons

    Eight shared channels — the community side of the system, where surplus flows back to the people in it. Described as a vision, not a commitment, and it stays that way until it is real.

    Read the Commons channels

A name and a way to reply are both optional; you can write to us as a person with no address, no documents, and nothing to prove.

Our privacy promise, in plain words

  • What we keep

    Only what you choose to send us, in an email in one mailbox, read by our team. Nothing on this page is saved — no account, no profile, no queue, no file about you.

  • What comes off this page

    Nothing. Your answers are worked out inside your own browser and never travel on their own. There is no tracking on this page and no analytics.

  • What we never do

    We never sell or share a list, never name our donors, never market to you, and never ask for documents, ID numbers, medical details, or immigration status.

  • How to be forgotten

    Reply to your own message and ask us to delete it. We delete it, and we tell you when it is done. Asking for nothing is a complete answer.
